pages.text: The $(item)Ionospheric Processor$() is the heart of a sounding station: a rack of glowing valves that sends pulses straight up through an $(item)Ionosonde Antenna$() and times the echoes off the sky.$(br2)With its ionosonde on the coax of its lower half it knows the solar weather; a comparator reads 1 (blackout) to 6 (great). Right click for its terminal.

pages.title: On the air
pages.text: Put a radio against the rack. Any $(l:radiocraft:sky/wefax)WEFAX$(/l) or $(l:radiocraft:digital/teletype)teletype$(/l) on that frequency that presses SOLR WX gets an answer under the rack's call sign (the placer's). Machines touching the rack or its radio read it directly.$(br2)$(thing)Blackout alerts$() (on unless switched off) warn a few minutes before a blackout: WEFAX receivers that hear one print it and beep.

pages.title: The terminal
pages.text: $(li)$(thing)[1] Timed bulletins$(): off by default. On, it also sends the report unasked: when it comes online, when the weather changes and every five minutes.$(li)$(thing)[2] Blackout alerts$(): the warnings, on by default.$(li)$(thing)[3] Send bulletin now$().$(br)It also shows its radio's frequency and any blackout forecast.

pages.title: The ionosonde
pages.text: The $(item)Ionosonde Antenna$() is two blocks tall and goes on coax like a J-pole. It is made for sounding, not talking: on a radio it matches poorly (SWR 3 on VHF, 8 on HF).$(br2)Making a processor takes an amethyst shard among its parts.
